title: Tapestry of Black Britons at the Hastings Museum
venue: Hastings Museum & Art Gallery, Bohemia Road, Hastings
summary: Paula Ogun Hector's five large-scale woven artworks, telling the story of almost 2,000 years of African and Caribbean presence in Britain, run at Hastings Museum & Art Gallery until 8 November. Local embroiderers and Hastings Academy students have also created a modern Hastings Bayeux for the exhibition. Entry and parking are free.

title: Kings Road Market
summary: The monthly street market returns to King's Road in Bohemia, with over 30 stalls selling vintage clothing, arts and crafts, handmade goods and local gifts among the area's independent shops, cafés and galleries.

title: Sarah Gillespie and Chris Montague at Mike's
summary: Sarah Gillespie and Chris Montague perform together at Mike's, playing from a new stripped-back duo album recorded in a cottage on the shores of Loch Fyne, as part of an album launch tour through Britain and the USA.

title: Veterans Hub social gathering
venue: The Veterans Hub, 45 Robertson Street, Hastings
summary: Open to all, after the 11am Remembrance Day service at the war memorial in Alexandra Park.

title: Rye Bonfire
summary: A torch-lit procession leaves Tilling Green and moves through the town, ending with a big bonfire on the Salts and fireworks, including a giant fire-breathing dragon called Scorch.

title: Robertsbridge Bonfire
summary: The town's procession moves through the High Street to end at the recreation ground, where a giant bonfire is lit and fireworks follow.
